analyst_view.overall: Early view: Köln have won one of their last seven league games and are short of strikers, with Thijs Dallinga out for the season and Ragnar Ache a doubt, so much depends on Saïd El Mala and his brother Malek. Elversberg have been the most impressive of the promoted sides under Vincent Wagner, with open games and goals from set pieces.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Köln's games have been low on goals (24 in nine) while Elversberg's have been high (35 in nine), and the number sits between the two. I stay with it.

corners.text: The site expects 11.4 corners, 7.4 of them Köln's. That is a lot for a side that had 41% of the ball and ten shots in the derby; even at home against a promoted side, I lean lower on Köln's share.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: Köln took six yellows in the derby and were part of a seven-card game at Union, with Linton Maina booked in both, a sign of a team that defends by fouling when under pressure.

shots.text: The site has 29.5 shots, 19.0 for Köln. With their main strikers out, 19 attempts looks high for Köln, who managed ten against Leverkusen. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. Fewer Köln shots would normally mean fewer on target, but Elversberg finish efficiently and the El Mala brothers have scored in each of Köln's last two league games, so I stay level.
